_label: RX-06 solver leg: read-decision misread channel (circuit_backends.CircuitChainSpin p_read_flip) on the Section 3.4.2 (ER14) and Section 3.3 (G1) protocols; all rows MEASURED solver output, the flip rate itself is derived from the RX-06 offset MC

as_committed.source: read_offset_mc_summary.json:misread_channel.as_committed.p_read_flip [effective margins measured on the as-committed deck (C_node=0 fF) with the in-situ offset statistics at that C_node]

conservative.source: read_offset_mc_summary.json:misread_channel.conservative.p_read_flip [static divider margins with the MC-IDEAL offset statistics; corresponds to a decoupled reference / damped sense node, i.e. no kickback help]

p_flip_cap_note: 0.5 is the maximum-entropy point of a binary flip channel (the reported state carries no information); requested multiples above it are capped, so a capped row is the worst physically meaningful case rather than the literal multiple
read_flip_arms_mode: none (no DAC quantization, no rail clip) so the degradation is attributable to the misread channel alone
dac_combined_note: RX-04 constraint: combining the read-flip channel with the DAC backend on G-set-scale instances requires rail half-width >= +/-10 V_T; +/-4 V_T sits in the p_s=0 regime. Arms use u_span=10, nbits=6, run as a no-flip / flip pair so the marginal cost of the misread is isolated.
stats: Wilson 95% CI on p_s; parametric-bootstrap 95% CI on TTS ratio vs the same-instance ideal arm (stats.py, RX-01 convention); bootstrap CI on the energy-median shift
